**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part**: Wheat/grass leaf (narrow, elongated blade)
- **Key features**: A single, prominent longitudinal stripe running the full length of the leaf — tan to brown in color at the center, with yellowish margins transitioning to green on the outer leaf edges
- **Pattern**: The stripe follows the vascular tissue (veins) and spans the entire visible leaf length
- **Texture**: Appears necrotic/bleached centrally, not powdery or pustular

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Cephalosporium Stripe**: Caused by *Cephalosporium gramineum*; produces distinct chlorotic (yellow) to tan/necrotic stripes running the full length of the leaf along vascular bundles — matches very well with the single wide longitudinal stripe seen here
- **Bacterial_Leaf_Streak / Bacterial_Streak**: Causes water-soaked then tan streaks following veins, but typically multiple narrow streaks rather than one wide central stripe
- **Stripe_Rust**: Yellow/orange powdery pustules in stripes — no pustules visible here
- **Tan_Spot**: More oval/diamond lesions with yellow halos, not a long linear stripe
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Irregular blotches, not this clean longitudinal stripe pattern

The single, wide, full-length tan/brown stripe following the leaf vasculature is the hallmark symptom of **Cephalosporium Stripe**.
